lines.li: [them] They still talk at home about {DEEDNAME}, and who saw it done.
[us] We were glad to help.
[them] It showed, and that's why I'm glad to be here.
[them] Some of ours camped by you once, and they came home with good things to say.
[us] They were good neighbors while they stayed.
[them,their:tribal] Then the path between our fires is worn smooth.
[them] Then we're square, and glad of it.
[them] Your welcome is still talked about at home.
[us] Only good things, I hope.
[them,their:medieval] Good things, and they get better every time they're told.
[them] Good things, and a few exaggerations.
[them] When there was talk of peace, your people helped it along.
[us] Somebody had to sit in the middle.
[them] Most would rather not, and we know it.
[them] You brought one of our children home, and no mother at home will forget it.
[us] We couldn't have done anything else.
[them,their:tribal] The child's name is sung with yours now, at every fire.
[them] Plenty would have, and you didn't.
[them] You mourned with us when we lost one of ours, and that was noticed.
[us] Grief shouldn't be carried alone.
[them] No, and you made it a little lighter.
[them] There's timber of yours in our walls now, and we know whose it is.
[us] I hope it holds.
[them] It holds, and so does the thanks.
[them] Your people went on the road for ours when it mattered.
[us] It's what neighbors do.
[them] Not all neighbors, believe me.
[them] Your warning reached us in time, and we were ready.
[us] I'm glad it arrived.
[them] So are we, and so are the ones who would have been in the way.
[them] One of yours beat one of ours in a fair fight, and we respect that.
[us] It was a hard fight.
[them,their:tribal] The best ones are, and they're sung about after.
[them] The fair ones always are.
[them] Word is you're fair people to trade with.
[us,trait:Greedy] Fair, mostly.
[us] We try to be.
[them] Keep trying, it brings the caravans back.
[them] Your people did right by mine when it would have been easier not to.
[us] We'd like to think you'd do the same.
[them] We would, and now we have a reason to.
[them,deedbest:tended] Which of you is {DEEDBY}, who tended {DEEDNAME}?
[them,deedbest:released] Which of you is {DEEDBY}, who let {DEEDNAME} go home?
[us] Why do you ask?
[them] Because at home they want to know what kind of person does that.
[them] You're the one who helped {YOURDEEDNAME}, aren't you?
[us] I am, how did you know?
[them,byyou:freed] Everyone at home knows who set {YOURDEEDNAME} free.
[them,byyou:tended,!byyou:freed] Everyone at home knows who mended {YOURDEEDNAME}.
[us] I didn't know anyone was counting.
[them] Somebody always is.
[them] I hope what we sent when you wrote was some use.
[us] It was, more than you know.
[them] Then it was worth the walk it took to bring it.
[them] One of ours taught one of yours a thing or two, I hear.
[us] And it stuck, mostly.
[them] Mostly is how all learning goes.
[them] When you needed help, our people came.
[us] And we haven't forgotten.
[them,their:empire] Good, the Empire never does.
[them] Good, neither have we.
[them] The land you sit on was ours to give, you know.
[us] We know, and we're grateful.
[them] Grateful is good, and remembering is better.
[them] Did what we brought you serve you well?
[us] It did, thank you.
[them] Then ask again, if there's something else.
[them] Some of our traders still won't take this road, after what happened.
[us] That was a bad time, for all of us.
[them] Maybe, but it was our goods that went missing.
[them] Some of ours were sold off by your people, and their families remember.
[us] I won't defend it.
[them] Good, I wouldn't want to hear you try.
[them] {WRONGNAME} died in your keeping, and their family still asks why.
[us] I wish I had an answer for them.
[them] So do they.
[them] Your people came against one of our towns once, and we haven't forgotten.
[us] And yet you're here.
[them] I'm here, and I'm watching.
[them] Your waste reaches farther than you think, people at home have noticed.
[us] We're working on it.
[them] Work faster, then.
[them] Someone here was rough with one of ours, and word got back.
[us] Words get heated, now and then.
[them] They do, and they travel faster than apologies.
[them] When we asked something of your people, we came away with less than we hoped.
[us] We can't always give what's asked.
[them] No, but people remember who did.
[them] Some of ours were sent packing from your land once.
[us] It was a hard choice.
[them] It was a hard walk home, too.
[them] When it came to it, your people didn't stand with ours.
[us] We did what we thought was right.
[them] Everyone always does.
[us] Your people have raided us before, you know.
[them,them:kind] Not with my blessing, and I'm sorry for it.
[them] Some of mine have, and I won't pretend otherwise.
[us] Then let's hope today is a better day.
[us] Your people killed one of ours once.
[them,them:kind] I know, and I wish I could undo it.
[them] I know, and I won't ask you to forget it.
[us] I won't.
[them] It's been quiet out here, I hear, no trouble for a good while.
[us] Don't say it out loud.
[them,their:tribal] Then I will say nothing, and the spirits won't hear.
[them] Sorry, I'll knock on something wooden.
[them] There are more of you than I expected.
[us] We keep growing.
[them] Careful, you'll be a town before you know it.
[them] Just a handful of you, out here on your own?
[us] A handful is enough, if it's the right handful.
[them] I'll give you that.
[them] You've done well for yourselves out here.
[us] We've been lucky, and stubborn.
[them] Mind the lucky part, it draws attention.
[them] It's a hard life out here, I can see.
[us] Hard, but ours.
[them] That counts for more than most people think.
[them] You're holding prisoners, I see.
[us] We are, for now.
[them,their:tribal] Treat them well, the spirits watch how captives are kept.
[them] I hope you keep them better than most do.
[them] You keep a lot of animals here.
[us,us:best:Animals] Most of them are my doing, I'm afraid.
[us] They earn their keep, mostly.
[them] The good ones always do.
[them] I hear your council talks everything over before anyone lifts a finger.
[us,us:speaker] It does, and I get to hear every word of it.
[us] It does, at length.
[them,their:tribal] So do our elders, so I won't laugh.
[them,their:empire] At home we would simply be told.
[them] Better than one voice shouting, I suppose.
[them] Did I just miss {DAY}?
[us] By a day or two, I'm afraid.
[them] Then I'll come earlier next year.
[them] I speak well of {COLONY} at home, you know.
[us] That's good to hear.
[them] Keep it so, and you'll never want for friends.
[them] I'll be honest, I don't know what to make of your people yet.
[us] Then stay a while and find out.
[them] A while, maybe.
[them] Who came at you, then?
[us,colony:raid:tribal] Tribesmen, and they fought hard.
[us] Raiders, and that's all I'll say about them.
[them] Fair enough, I won't ask more.
[them] A baby on the way here, I hear, tell them to sleep while they can.
[us] Is that your advice as a parent?
[them] It's my only advice, and nobody ever takes it.
